description: Append-oriented empirical history of HumanityAI operational system-design experiments and changes. This file records observed outcomes and interpretations but grants no authority and cannot override protected governance, security, licensing, constitutional, scheduler, or permission boundaries.

records.problem_trigger: Low decision progress relative to compute and overlapping allocation/verification responsibilities.
records.prior_design: Peer-like adaptive workers with diffuse ordinary management/integration ownership.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Separate management, production, verification and assurance to improve decision delta while preserving independence.
records.exact_change: Human/constitution -> D controller -> A/B operators -> independent C verifier -> independent Audit; risk-tiered integration and durable portfolio state.

observed_outcomes.observation: C qualification changed early integration and allocation decisions.

lessons: Consume adverse C verdicts as control signals; do not declare hierarchy proven prematurely.

records.problem_trigger: Need evidence of end-to-end producer -> C -> D throughput.
records.prior_design: One C QUALIFY block but no completed Tier-2 integration cycle.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Independent PASS plus exact-head CI should permit safe integration.
records.exact_change: PR #84 independently PASSed and was integrated through the normal path; no authority changed.
records.evaluation_window: Several additional cycles and Audit observation.

observed_outcomes.observation: First end-to-end Tier-2 integration cycle completed.

records.problem_trigger: Audit #111 and controller runs exposed stale assignments, duplicate work, freshness rework and queue aging.
records.prior_design: Durable portfolio without mandatory post-integration coherence gate or hard Tier-2 WIP limit.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Finish-before-start, WIP<=2, live reconciliation and explicit assignment contracts should reduce stale/duplicate work.
records.exact_change: Adopted human-approved coherence gate and Audit #111 flow standard without changing scheduler, permissions, C independence or Audit authority.
evaluation_criteria: Completed work removed before replacement allocation

observed_outcomes.observation: Reconciliation repeatedly held replacement work while queues were congested.

failures_side_effects: Several windows were consumed by reconciliation/freshness work.
lessons: Keep reconciliation small and tied to allocation changes; record mandatory checkpoints promptly.

records.problem_trigger: A bounded P05 Tier-2 assignment released after flow-control remediation failed to materialize as any producer-ready candidate across multiple healthy controller checks, leaving zero active Tier-2 WIP and forcing a mandatory production hold because the failure itself had not been recorded.
records.prior_design: D could release one bounded Tier-2 assignment after coherence reconciliation, relying on A/B fallback autonomy and subsequent live PR state to make producer readiness observable.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Treating invisible/non-materialized assignments as a process failure, requiring an explicit checkpoint before reallocation, and preferring observable producer-ready state should prevent repeated reissuance of work that silently consumes slots without decision delta.
records.exact_change: No authority or scheduler change. D withdrew the aged P05 release, held all new Tier-2 production, required this append-oriented checkpoint, and directed available compute to read-only synthesis until live state can be reconciled after the checkpoint becomes canonical. Replacement P05 work is not automatically reissued.
expected_benefit: Make assignment failure observable before consuming more Tier-2 capacity
Force reassessment of P05 value rather than reflexive retry
risks: Production hold can leave useful producer capacity idle
A checkpoint can itself become bureaucracy if delayed
PR state alone may not reveal why an assignment failed to materialize
records.evaluation_window: Next 3-6 healthy D cycles after this checkpoint is canonical.
evaluation_criteria: No new Tier-2 work is released before a fresh live-state coherence check
At most one bounded candidate is released after the hold
Released work becomes producer-ready or is explicitly killed within two healthy D cycles
No duplicate P05 assignment is created
Controller/recovery toil declines rather than adding coordination layers

observed_outcomes.observation: Canonical portfolio at main 1e8f4bd6d9dc7599f468bb90d243537a006121eb reports zero active Tier-2 WIP, only deferred PR #70, and an aged P05 assignment with no candidate.
Repeated reconciliation retained the production hold instead of silently reallocating new Tier-2 work.
The failure is more consistent with an observability/flow problem than evidence that P05 itself is low value; causal diagnosis remains uncertain.

failures_side_effects: Multiple controller windows produced little new mission decision delta while the checkpoint remained overdue.
The safeguard became a source of idle capacity because institutional memory was not updated promptly.
lessons: An assignment is not successful allocation until producer-ready state becomes observable.
Do not repeatedly reissue invisible work; kill or reassess it after two healthy cycles.
Mandatory design-memory checkpoints must be small and prompt so the control itself does not dominate capacity.
After this checkpoint merges, reconcile live state before deciding whether P05 still dominates read-only alternatives.
